words_to_read_new.meaning: ord means order - the way things are arranged, one after another
add -ly: doing things in a neat order
dis means apart, so disorder is order that has come apart - a mess
re means again: to put things back in order again
in the usual order of things, so it means normal
the numbers that tell order: 1st, 2nd, 3rd
co means together: to put plans in order together
sub means under: placed under someone in the order
extra means beyond: beyond the usual order - amazing
to officially put someone into their place in the order; to appoint
an official rule that keeps everything in order
in- means not: not accepting your place under the order

sessions.wtr_new_notes:
Teacher script - read each line aloud as the word appears. Name every part, then fuse the parts into the meaning, the way sub (beneath) + marine (water) fuses into a vessel beneath the water.
**order** - ord is the root on its own, order: things arranged in their places, one after another.
**orderly** - ord means order + -ly means in that way: doing things in an ordered way. Neat.
**disorder** - dis- means apart + ord means order: the order pulled apart. A mess!
**reorder** - re- means again + ord means order: to put things back into order again.
**ordinary** - ordin means order + -ary means relating to: relating to the usual order of things. Normal, nothing special.
**ordinal** - ordin means order + -al means to do with: the numbers to do with order - 1st, 2nd, 3rd.
**coordinate** - co- means together + ordin means order + -ate means to do it: to bring people or plans into order together.
**subordinate** - sub- means under + ordin means order + -ate describes the person: someone placed under another in the order.
**extraordinary** - extra- means beyond + ordin means order + -ary means relating to: beyond the usual order. Amazing.
**ordain** - ord means order: to officially place someone into the order. To appoint them.
**ordinance** - ordin means order + -ance turns it into a thing: a rule made to keep order.
**insubordinate** - in- means not + sub- means under + ordin means order: refusing to sit under your place in the order.
**Memory hook:** every ord word is about things lined up in their place. Hear ORD, think "Off to my place in the line." Students say the hook with you, then whisper it to a partner.
sessions.extension: Once finished, write one sentence using two ord words joined by a subordinating clause. Reminder: a subordinating clause starts with a joining word like because, although or while, and cannot stand alone. Stretch: open your sentence with the subordinating clause and follow it with a comma.

new_morph_activity.title: Build an ord word
new_morph_activity.rule: Word building: take the root ord/ordin and add morphemes you know.
new_morph_activity.example: dis + ord + er        re + ord + er        ordin + ary        co + ordin + ate
items: Build three REAL ord words on your whiteboard.
Then write one sentence with your best word that shows its meaning.
new_morph_activity.notes:
1. SAY: The root is the engine. Add prefixes and suffixes you know and build me three real ord words. TIME: 2 minutes building, 1 minute for the sentence. CIRCULATE: check the morphemes are real, not invented. SCAN boards up together, pick two students to read their sentence aloud. TRAP: bolting on morphemes that make non-words, like ordful. Fix: say the word aloud - if we never say it, we do not build it; student swaps the suffix and rebuilds. STRETCH: build a 4-morpheme word (insubordinate, coordination). HELP: start from order and add ONE prefix (dis-, re-).
---
Purpose: Yoshimoto word building - students own the morphemes before spelling from them. [You Do | Word building | Morphology]

i_do.title: Colons introduce a list
i_do.rule: A colon says: here comes the list I promised. It may only follow a complete sentence.
i_do.example: Pack your bag: a hat, your lunch, a water bottle.
items: Cover the list with your hand. 'Pack your bag' can stand alone - so the colon is legal.
Two dots, full sentence first, list after.
i_do.routine: Eyes on me - watch the test
i_do.notes:
1. SAY: A colon is a signpost. It tells the reader a list is coming right now. 2. MODEL: point at the example. Think aloud: 'Pack your bag' is a full sentence, so I am allowed the colon. 3. COVER the list with your hand, read the first half aloud, SAY: it stands alone, colon legal. TRAP: colon after a fragment like 'You need:'. Fix: cover the colon, student reads what is left aloud, says whether it stands alone, rewrites.

we_do.footer: Stem: The colon belongs there because ...
we_do.notes:
ANSWER: Every athlete needs three things: courage, practice and rest. 1. SAY: Write the sentence and place the colon where it belongs. 20 sec, boards up together. 2. SCAN boards, back row first. 80%+ correct -> You do. Less -> cover the list together, read the first half aloud, re-ask with boards. 3. ASK: How do you know the colon is legal there? EXPECT: the first part is a complete sentence. Stem: The colon belongs there because ...

words_to_read_new.meaning: doing things in a neat order
the ceremony of officially putting someone into their place in the order
co means together: to bring plans into order together
-tion turns the verb into a thing: parts working in order together
dis means apart: behaving with the order gone
being placed under someone in the order
pre means before: to set the order before it happens
-ly makes it how you do it: in a way beyond the usual order
in- means not: refusing your place under the order

sessions.wtr_new_notes:
Teacher script - yesterday's root, bigger words. Name every part, then fuse the parts into the meaning, like sub (beneath) + marine (water) = a vessel beneath the water.
**orderly** - ord means order + -ly means in that way: doing things in an ordered way.
**ordination** - ordin means order + -ation makes it an event: the ceremony of officially placing someone into the order.
**coordinate** - co- means together + ordin means order + -ate means to do it: to bring plans into order together.
**coordination** - co- together + ordin order + -ation makes it a thing: parts working together in order. Your PE coordination!
**disorderly** - dis- means apart + ord means order + -ly means in that way: behaving with the order pulled apart.
**subordination** - sub- means under + ordin means order + -ation makes it a thing: being placed under someone in the order.
**preordain** - pre- means before + ord means order: to set the order before it even happens.
**extraordinarily** - extra- beyond + ordin order + -ary relating to + -ly in that way: in a way beyond the usual order.
**insubordination** - in- not + sub- under + ordin order + -ation a thing: refusing your place under the order. Four parts stacked!
**Memory hook:** same as yesterday - hear ORD, think "Off to my place in the line." Ask: who can build the LONGEST ord word from memory? EXPECT: insubordination - in + sub + ordin + ation.
sessions.extension: Once finished, write the meaning of subordinate in your own words using the meanings of sub- (under) and ord (order). Stretch: do the same for insubordination - it has three morphemes to unpack.

new_morph_activity.title: Morpheme sums
new_morph_activity.rule: I say the meaning sum, you build the ord word in your OG workbook.
new_morph_activity.example: together + order + to do = ?      not + under + order = ?      before + order = ?
items: Write the word AND its morpheme sum beside it.
Swap workbooks with your partner: do the parts match the meaning?
new_morph_activity.footer: Stretch: write your own sum for a partner
new_morph_activity.notes:
ANSWER: coordinate, insubordination (accept insubordinate), preordain. 1. SAY: I give you the meaning sum, you build the ord word and write the sum beside it. TIME: 3 minutes in workbooks. 2. Read each sum aloud twice while students build. CIRCULATE: the sum must sit beside the word - the sum is the thinking. 3. Partners swap and check the parts against the meanings. TRAP: writing the word without its sum. Fix: student says the sum aloud, then writes it beside the word. STRETCH: invent a new ord sum for a partner to solve. HELP: word bank in the board corner - coordinate, preordain, insubordination.
---

i_do.title: Colon or no colon?
